solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: He interrupts politician with an idea

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle, so the first word is set inside the politician

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cuts in while a politician is speaking because they have had a bright idea.
explanation.walkthrough: TORY is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypothesis or notion put forward is a synonym for an idea.

clue.text: Boring ties — more variety is needed

indicators.note: calling for variety means the letters must be mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A fashion complaint: neckties are dull and need more variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious or dull things are boring.

clue.text: Someone must have been been willing to appoint her

definitions.text: Someone must have been been willing to appoint her

parts.words: Someone must have been been willing to appoint her
parts.note: 'willing' hides the making of a will, the document that names a woman to carry it out

explanation.surface: It reads like someone agreeing to give a woman a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'willing' means making a will, not being keen.
explanation.definitionFit: The woman named in a will to carry out its terms holds this title, the female form of executor.

clue.text: It can be taken in a bank

definitions.meaning: sailors take in part of a sail to shorten it in strong wind
a ridge of rock or sand just below the surface of the sea

explanation.surface: It sounds like money being paid in at a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a shortened section of sail and an underwater ridge of rock or coral.

clue.text: Unremittingly faithful?

definitions.meaning: unceasing, never letting up; the clue's adverb stands loosely for the adjective

explanation.surface: A description of a devoted partner who never wavers.
explanation.walkthrough: Not a strict double definition: 'Unremittingly' is an adverb while the answer is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both never stopping and staying loyal.

clue.text: Colonel possibly in command in present situation

indicators.note: the abbreviation for in command sits in the middle of the word for present

parts.note: to offer something is to present it
IC is short for in charge or in command

explanation.surface: A colonel might take charge in the current situation.
explanation.walkthrough: IC, as in second-in-command (2IC), stands for in command; 'situation' only completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is one example of a commissioned military rank holder.

clue.text: A cross can't be played with — it's very holy

indicators.note: letters that are played with are toyed with and moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A crucifix is too sacred to be treated as a toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too sacred to be touched or violated is utterly holy.

clue.text: Farewell notice that is going to university

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
i.e. is short for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A student puts up a goodbye notice before leaving for university.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for goodbye is used in English as a farewell.

clue.text: It may be prescribed or inscribed

definitions.text: It may be prescribed or inscribed

parts.words: It may be prescribed or inscribed
parts.note: a doctor prescribes a pill; a stone slab can carry carved writing

explanation.surface: It reads like a rule that can be laid down or written.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a pill from a doctor and a flat slab bearing an inscription.

clue.text: They're not the original apes

definitions.meaning: to ape someone is to imitate them

explanation.surface: These apes are not the first of their kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Duplicates are not originals, and imitating someone is the verb sense of the same word.

clue.text: School subject — English — started, was able to recite fluently

parts.note: RE is religious education, a subject taught in British schools
to have led off is to have started or opened proceedings

explanation.surface: A pupil starts on a lesson and then recites it smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is a standard subject in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel something off is an idiom for reciting a list quickly and without hesitation.

clue.text: Conservative member to go on to higher things

parts.note: a limb, such as an arm or leg, is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A Conservative party member hopes to rise to a better position.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend or rise, literally or in career terms, is to go on to higher things.

clue.text: Avoid getting hot in a blazer

indicators.note: the letter for hot is placed in the middle of the word for the blazer

parts.note: the sun is a blazer, something that blazes in the sky
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone turns down wearing a jacket because it is too hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blazer' looks like a jacket, but here it is the blazing sun.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep away from or steer clear of someone is a synonym for avoiding them.

clue.text: An opening revelation

definitions.meaning: an opening up or uncovering of something
a making known of a secret

explanation.surface: It reads like the first big twist of a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like 'first', but it is a definition: an uncovering.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name the act of uncovering, and the thing so made public.

clue.text: Not in favour of rigid price control for winter motoring

parts.note: to be anti something is to be against it
a price freeze is a government ban on raising prices

explanation.surface: A motorist opposes rigid price controls on winter fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A coolant added to car radiators stops them icing up, so it is needed for winter driving.

clue.text: Servicemen seen in the airmen's mess

indicators.note: making a mess of the letters jumbles them, and an airmen's mess also suggests their dining hall

parts.note: the letters of the word taken as written, the S included

explanation.surface: Members of another service turn up in the airmen's dining hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' looks like the military dining room, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers serving at sea and ashore in naval corps are servicemen.

clue.text: Actually, it's about a friend

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in letters
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone explains what something is actually about: a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs meaning in fact or truly.

clue.text: On the side of the junior partner

parts.note: a junior arrives later, being younger
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: A firm's junior partner takes sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideways or from the side is the meaning of this adverb.

clue.text: One to vilify a British resident

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to slander is to vilify

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to smear a person living in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain is made up of isles, so anyone living there lives on an island.

clue.text: Tax being cut

definitions.meaning: a duty charged on goods made within a country
to remove by cutting out, as a surgeon does

explanation.surface: A tax is being reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a duty levied on home goods; the verb means to cut out.

clue.text: All together in France

parts.note: a French phrase used in English meaning as one body

explanation.surface: It sounds like a group touring France.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase meaning as a whole group, all at once.

clue.text: Finds nothing in a ruined castle

indicators.note: the letter for nothing goes inside the rearranged castle
a ruined castle is broken apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An explorer finds nothing inside a crumbling castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' turns CASTLE into LCATES, and 'in' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To find the place of something is to pinpoint it, a synonym of discovering.

clue.text: Ships in river south of the Equator

parts.note: sailors call the Equator the line

explanation.surface: Vessels sailing on a river in the southern hemisphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south of' places S after R in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Large passenger vessels on regular routes are ships.

clue.text: Fail to correspond?

parts.note: not writing letters seems meant, but the sense is not matching or agreeing

explanation.surface: It sounds like neglecting to write letters to a pen pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspond' suggests letter-writing, but here it means to match.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unlike or disagree is to fail to match, the other sense of correspond.

clue.text: Orchestrate popular march to entertain the troops

parts.note: IN means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: to strut is to march or walk proudly
men are troops, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A bandleader arranges a popular march to cheer up soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orchestrate' is used here as a verb, to arrange or engineer, matching the verb sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to arrange music for an orchestra or to engineer an outcome is to orchestrate.

clue.text: It can't run, so takes cover

parts.note: a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot run away hides under cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that is firm, not liquid, cannot run or flow.

clue.text: A touching article or tract

parts.note: RE means touching on or concerning
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A short piece of writing about something touching, or a pamphlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tract' looks like a pamphlet, but here it means a stretch of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of land or region is a tract.

clue.text: I'd look up to see a star

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: lo is an old word for look

explanation.surface: Someone says they would look up to a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero worshipped by fans, such as a pop celebrity, is a star.

clue.text: Falls short of a pound note — forged perhaps

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: L stands for a pound, from the Latin libra
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A banknote is a forgery and falls short of its full value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of a pound' drops one L from FALLS, giving FALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forged is fake, an example of what is not genuine.

clue.text: Stood on both sides

parts.note: standing with a leg on each side of something, or backing both sides of an argument at once

explanation.surface: It reads like a fence-sitter who refuses to pick a side.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit or stand astride, legs apart over something, or to favour both camps, is this verb.

clue.text: Having paid, he [he] recovers

definitions.meaning: one who has paid off a debt or a ransom
one who wins something back, such as a pawned item

explanation.surface: Someone settles a debt and gets their goods back.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed [he] marks that the word 'he' serves both definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who buys back a pledge, or Christ as the one who paid for sins, is so called.

clue.text: He may make or interpret a score

definitions.text: He may make or interpret a score

parts.words: He may make or interpret a score
parts.note: a sportsman scores points; a musician reads and performs from a musical score

explanation.surface: It sounds like a composer or a conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a score' points to sport, 'interpret a score' to music.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportsman scores in a match and a musician performs music written in a score.
